target.title: fix(codex): rotate bounded-turn auth profiles on usage limits
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Bounded Codex app-server turns (image understanding via the `image` tool, structured extraction, hosted web search) pin every call to the first profile in the auth failover order (`resolveAuthProfileOrder(...)[0]`) and never record usage-limit blocks. When that profile exhausts its Codex subscription quota:

- every bounded turn keeps re-selecting the same blocked profile and fails until the weekly reset, even when other configured profiles still have quota, and
- because the block is never persisted to `usageStats`, the order resolver has no way to learn the profile is unusable and move it behind healthy ones.

Regular chat attempts already handle this (`markCodexAuthProfileBlockedFromRateLimits` + cooldown-aware profile ordering); the bounded-turn path was missing both halves.

We hit this in production: a gateway with two OpenAI profiles (`auth.order: { openai: ["openai:A", "openai:B"] }`) had profile A exhaust its weekly Codex quota. Chat turns kept working on profile B, but every `image` tool call failed for two days straight with `codex/gpt-5.5: You've hit your usage limit. … try again at Jul 11th` while profile B sat idle with quota available.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runBoundedCodexAppServerTurn` now:

1. **Marks the failing profile blocked** when a bounded turn fails with a usage-limit error, using the same `markAuthProfileBlockedUntil` + Codex-advertised reset time mechanism as the chat run-attempt path. The marking happens while the per-attempt client is still open so the failing profile's rate limits can be read, and it trusts rate-limit payloads the same way the chat path does (error payload, or cache updates observed after this turn's `turn/start` began). Callers that don't supply an `authProfileStore` (hosted web search) persist the block through the agent-dir store.
2. **Walks the remaining eligible profiles in failover order** (capped at 3 attempts, sharing one deadline so retries never extend the caller's timeout budget). A caller-pinned profile stays pinned (single attempt, still records the block), and native Codex auth (`homeScope: "user"`) keeps its current single-attempt behavior since no profiles apply there.
3. **Preserves Codex error metadata on bounded-turn failures** (added after ClawSweeper's review): failed `turn/completed` events and `error` notifications now attach the Codex error payload (`data.error` with `codexErrorInfo`) in the same shape as RPC failures, so usage-limit classification does not depend on message text. `usageLimitExceeded` variants whose message never says "usage limit" (workspace credits / spend-cap wording) now rotate and block correctly.

The error surfaced on the final failure is the reset-aware `CodexBoundedTurnUsageLimitError` ("You've reached your Codex subscription usage limit. Next reset …") instead of the raw provider message.

**Stored data model note:** no new persisted schema — the bounded path writes the same `usageStats` fields (`blockedUntil`, `blockedReason`, `blockedSource`, `blockedModel`, `failureCounts`) the chat path already writes via `markAuthProfileBlockedUntil`, and reads go through the existing cooldown-aware order resolver. No migration required.

## User Impact

Multi-profile setups (e.g. a Pro account plus a backup account) no longer lose image understanding, structured extraction, and hosted web search for days when one profile hits its Codex subscription limit — bounded turns fail over to the next profile with quota, and the blocked profile is skipped by ordering everywhere until its advertised reset time. Single-profile setups see no behavior change other than a clearer, reset-aware error message.

## Evidence

### Live before/after proof (real usage-limited account)

Environment: macOS gateway host, auth store with two OpenAI OAuth profiles in `auth.order` (`openai:A` first, `openai:B` second). Profile A's Codex **weekly quota is genuinely exhausted upstream** (resets Jul 11); profile B is healthy. Both runs use the same isolated state dir (`--profile proof`, a copy of the production store with no block markers) and the same tiny local test image, model pinned to `codex/gpt-5.5`.

**Before — openclaw 2026.6.11 release binary (single-profile pin, no rotation):**

```console
$ openclaw --profile proof infer image describe --file test-red.png \
    --model codex/gpt-5.5 --prompt "What color? One word." --json
Error: You've hit your usage limit. Visit https://chatgpt.com/codex/settings/usage
to purchase more credits or try again at Jul 11th, 2026 10:55 AM.
```

**After — this branch (`pnpm build`, `node openclaw.mjs`), same command, same state:**

```console
$ node openclaw.mjs --profile proof infer image describe --file test-red.png \
    --model codex/gpt-5.5 --prompt "What color is this image? One word." --json --log-level info
[agent/embedded] codex bounded turn hit a usage limit; rotating auth profile
{
  "ok": true,
  "capability": "image.describe",
  "transport": "local",
  "provider": "codex",
  "model": "gpt-5.5",
  "attempts": [],
  "outputs": [
    { "path": ".../test-red.png", "text": "Red", "provider": "codex", "model": "gpt-5.5", "kind": "image.description" }
  ]
}
```

The rotation log line is emitted by the new bounded-turn loop after profile A's live usage-limit rejection; the successful describe ran on profile B. Reproduced twice.

**Production incident excerpt (before-fix behavior this PR removes)** — gateway 2026.6.11, every bounded image call for ~2 days (44 failures on the final day), URLs redacted:

```
[tools] image failed: All image models failed (2): codex/gpt-5.5: You've hit your usage limit.
Visit https://chatgpt.com/codex/settings/usage to purchase more credits or try again at
Jul 11th, 2026 10:55 AM. | google/gemini-3-flash-preview: … (429): You exceeded your current quota …
```

### Tests and gates

- New tests in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/bounded-turn.test.ts` (7) cover: rotation to the next profile on usage limit with `blockedUntil` persisted for the failing profile only; block persistence through the agent-dir store when no `authProfileStore` is supplied; trusting rate-limit updates received during turn start; **failed `turn/completed` usage-limit classification via preserved `codexErrorInfo` when the message contains no "usage limit" text**; pinned-profile behavior (no rotation, block still recorded, reset-aware error); timeout budget shared across rotation attempts; no rotation for non-usage-limit failures.
- `pnpm test:extension codex`: 97 files / 2006 tests pass. `pnpm check` and `pnpm build` pass.
- `codex review --base upstream/main` run locally across iterations; earlier findings (persist blocks for store-less callers, trust turn-start rate-limit cache updates, shared timeout budget, preserve failed-turn metadata) each addressed with code + tests.

### Known pre-existing limitation observed while producing the proof (not introduced here)

`markAuthProfileBlockedUntil` persists through the agent-dir store and silently no-ops when the failing profile is only inherited from the main agent's store (its lock updater requires the profile to exist in the agent-local persisted store). The existing chat run-attempt path has the same behavior. In such setups the in-call rotation added here still recovers every bounded turn (the exhausted profile fails fast and the turn proceeds on the next profile); making block persistence work for inherited profiles looks like a separate fix — happy to file a follow-up issue.
